arxiv-2103-12169.title: A Pilot Study For Fragment Identification Using 2D NMR and Deep Learning
arxiv-2103-12169.creator: Stefan Kuhn, Eda Tumer, Simon Colreavy-Donnelly, Ricardo Moreira Borges
arxiv-2103-12169.description: Abstract This paper presents a method to identify substructures in NMR spectra of mixtures, specifically 2D spectra, using a bespoke image-based Convolutional Neural Network application. This is done using HSQC and HMBC spectra separately and in combination. The application can reliably detect substructures in pure compounds, using a simple network.

arxiv-2211-14345.title: The Hubble Constant Troubled by Dark Matter in Non-Standard Cosmologies
arxiv-2211-14345.creator: J. S. Alcaniz 1,†, J. P. Neto 2,3,4,‡, F. S. Queiroz 3,4,5,§, D. R. da Silva 6,∗, R. Silva 2,3,¶
arxiv-2211-14345.description: Abstract The Standard Cosmological Model has experienced tremendous success at reproducing observational data by assuming a universe dominated by a cosmological constant and dark matter in a flat geometry. However, several studies, based on local measurements, indicate that the universe is expanding too fast, in disagreement with the Cosmic Microwave Background.

arxiv-2302-01786.title: Customer Profiling, Segmentation, and Sales Prediction using AI in Direct Marketing
arxiv-2302-01786.creator: Mahmoud SalahEldin Kasem, Mohamed Hamada, Islam Taj-Eddin
arxiv-2302-01786.description: Abstract In an increasingly customer-centric business environment, effective communication between marketing and senior management is crucial for success. With the rise of globalization and increased competition, utilizing new data mining techniques to identify potential customers is essential for direct marketing efforts.

arxiv-2307-01721.title: Nonlinearities in Long-Range Compact Michelson Interferometers
arxiv-2307-01721.creator: Jiri Smetana *, Chiara Di Fronzo, Anthony Amorosi, Denis Martynov
arxiv-2307-01721.description: Abstract Compact Michelson interferometers are well positioned to replace existing displacement sensors in the readout of seismometers and suspension systems, such as those used in contemporary gravitational-wave detectors. Here, we continue our previous investigation of a customised compact displacement sensor built by SmarAct, which operated on the principle of deep frequency modulation.

arxiv-2307-08748.title: Unconventional superfluidity and quantum geometry of topological bosons
arxiv-2307-08748.creator: Ilya Lukin, Andrii Sotnikov, Alexander Kruchkov
arxiv-2307-08748.description: Abstract We investigate superfluidity of bosons in gapped topological bands and discover a new phase that has no counterparts in the previous literature. This phase is characterized by a highly unconventional modulation of the order parameter, breaking the crystallographic symmetry, and for which the condensation momentum is neither zero nor any other high-symmetry vector of the Brillouin zone.

arxiv-2312-01600.title: A phenomenological model for interstitial hydrogen absorption in niobium
arxiv-2312-01600.creator: Arvind Ramachandran, Houlong Zhuang, Klaus S. Lackner
arxiv-2312-01600.description: Abstract A phenomenological model has been developed for hydrogen absorption in niobium. The model has 9 free parameters that have a physical basis. The model provides an excellent fit to the highly accurate isotherm data by Veleckis et al. and has been cross validated by limiting the fitting procedure to a training set.

arxiv-2407-17174.title: NarrationDep: Narratives on Social Media For Automatic Depression Detection
arxiv-2407-17174.creator: Hamad Zogan 1 , Imran Razzak 2 , Shoaib Jameel 3 , Guandong Xu 1
arxiv-2407-17174.description: Abstract . Social media posts provide valuable insight into the narrative of users and their intentions, including providing an opportunity to automatically model whether a social media user is depressed or not. The challenge lies in faithfully modelling user narratives from their online social media posts, which could potentially be useful in several different applications.

arxiv-2412-04352.title: Emergent Weyl-like points in periodically modulated systems
arxiv-2412-04352.creator: Fang Qin, Rui Chen
arxiv-2412-04352.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fang Qin, Rui Chen. We investigate a three-dimensional (3D) topological phase resembling a Weyl semimetal, modulated by a periodic potential and engineered through Floquet dynamics. This system is constructed by stacking two-dimensional Chern insulators and hosts Weyl-like points defined in the parameter space ( k x , k y , z ) (k_{x},k_{y},z) , distinct from conventional Weyl points in momentum space ( k x , k y , k z ) (k_{x},k_{y},k_{z}) .

arxiv-2509-01578.title: On Hom-Analogues of Heaps and Trusses
arxiv-2509-01578.creator: Tarik Anowar, Ripan Saha, Sayan Thokdar 1. Department of Mathematics, Raiganj University, Raiganj 733134, West Bengal, India2. Department of Mathematics, Raiganj University, Raiganj 733134, West Bengal, India3. Department of Mathematics, Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER-Pune
arxiv-2509-01578.description: Abstract ABSTRACT This paper develops the foundations of Hom-heaps , Hom-trusses , and Hom-braces as natural Hom-type analogues of their classical counterparts. We establish the correspondence between Hom-heaps and Hom-groups, showing that the retract of a Hom-heap at a point yields a Hom-group precisely when the point is fixed under the twisting map.

arxiv-2601-20868.title: Rethinking LLM-Driven Heuristic Design: Generating Efficient and Specialized Solvers via Dynamics-Aware Optimization
arxiv-2601-20868.creator: Rongzheng Wang, Yihong Huang, Muquan Li, Jiakai Li, Di Liang, Bob Simons, Pei Ke, Shuang Liang, Ke Qin, [0.6ex] University of Electronic Science, Technology of China
arxiv-2601-20868.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced the field of Combinatorial Optimization through automated heuristic generation. Instead of relying on manual design, this LLM-Driven Heuristic Design (LHD) process leverages LLMs to iteratively generate and refine solvers to achieve high performance.

arxiv-2602-07778.title: Attn-GS: Attention-Guided Context Compression for Efficient Personalized LLMs
arxiv-2602-07778.creator: Shenglai Zeng, Tianqi Zheng, Chuan Tian, Dante Everaert, Yau-Shian Wang, Yupin Huang, Michael J. Morais, Rohit Patki, Jinjin Tian, Xinnan Dai, Kai Guo, Monica Xiao Cheng, Hui Liu, Michigan State University
arxiv-2602-07778.description: Abstract Personalizing large language models (LLMs) to individual users requires incorporating extensive interaction histories and profiles, but input token constraints make this impractical due to high inference latency and API costs. Existing approaches rely on heuristic methods such as selecting recent interactions or prompting summarization models to compress user profiles.

arxiv-2603-15127.title: A Data-Driven Regional Model for Skillful Medium Range Typhoon Prediction
arxiv-2603-15127.creator: Zeyi Niu, Wei Huang, Sirong Huang, Zhuo Wang, Mu Mu, Mengqi Yang, Xinhai Han, Haofei Sun, Zhaoyang Huo, Bo Qin

plos-pone-0006557.title: Brief Subthreshold Events Can Act as Hebbian Signals for Long-Term Plasticity
plos-pone-0006557.creator: Elodie Fino, Jean-Michel Deniau, Laurent Venance
plos-pone-0006557.description: PLOS ONE research article. Action potentials are thought to be determinant for the induction of long-term synaptic plasticity, the cellular basis of learning and memory. However, neuronal activity does not lead systematically to an action potential but also, in many cases, to synaptic depolarizing subthres

pmc-10585155.title: When I feel that I am better off, science seems to make the world better off too: inequality, perceived standard of living and perceptions toward science
pmc-10585155.creator: Seungwoo Han, Yookyung Lee
pmc-10585155.description: The COVID-19 pandemic has underscored that divisive views on science and technology span both the Global North and South. This study posits that an individual’s perception of their current living standard acts as a mediating factor linking income inequality to attitudes towards scientific and technological advancements.

pmc-10628252.title: Bipolar neutrosophic WINGS for green technology innovation
pmc-10628252.creator: Yuan Tian, Kecheng Zhang
pmc-10628252.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Green technology innovation is a crucial assurance of achieving sustainable economic and environmental development, so improving the capability of green technology innovation is an urgent problem. In order to provide a more objective and accurate tool for identifying the most important impact factor of green technology innovation, this study innovatively proposes a new method by combining the bipolar neutrosophic sets with Weighted Influence Nonlinear Gauge System (WINGS) method. Furthermore, this paper intends to provide recommendations in improving green technology innovation capability.

pmc-11641256.title: Investigation of Silver- and Plant Extract-Infused Polymer Systems: Antioxidant Properties and Kinetic Release
pmc-11641256.creator: Magdalena Bańkosz, Bożena Tyliszczak
pmc-11641256.description: This study evaluated the impact of silver particles, suspended in Arnica montana flower extract, on the physicochemical characteristics and release dynamics of antioxidant compounds in PVP (polyvinylpyrrolidone)-based hydrogel systems. The hydrogels were synthesized via photopolymerization with fixed amounts of crosslinker (PEGDA) and photoinitiator, while the concentration of the silver-infused extract was systematically varied.

pmc-12613612.title: Juvenile dermatomyositis: new insights into pathogenesis and clinical applications
pmc-12613612.creator: Pauline PL Chan Ng, Aris E Syntakas, Lucy R Wedderburn
pmc-12613612.description: BackgroundJuvenile dermatomyositis (JDM), the most common inflammatory myopathy of childhood, is a complex autoimmune condition with significant disease burden and variable treatment responses. While conventional immunosuppression remains standard, advances in immunopathology are revealing new therapeutic and biomarker opportunities.Main bodyThis review provides emerging insights into JDM pathogenesis.

pmc-12625253.title: Neighborhood environmental burden and the elderly’s complete edentulism prevalence in the US
pmc-12625253.creator: Yang Liu, Xuewei Huang, Lijin Lin, Yuanyuan Cao, Jing Cheng, Fang Lei, Ke-Qiong Deng, Bo Cheng
pmc-12625253.description: BackgroundComplete edentulism affects the quality of life and overall health. Identifying environmental factors linked to teeth lost may help address the global public health burden of oral health. This study aimed to estimate the association between neighborhood-level cumulative environmental burden and the prevalence of complete edentulism among the elderly across the US.

pmc-12817539.title: Mesenchymal stem cell therapy for radiation-induced xerostomia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-12817539.creator: Shen-sui Li, Xu-dong Tian, Ju-kun Song, Ya-dong Wu, Wei-li Wang, Zheng-long Tang
pmc-12817539.description: BackgroundRadiation-induced xerostomia (RIX) is a frequent, debilitating complication of head and neck radiotherapy for cancer. Preclinical studies suggest that mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) may protect and regenerate salivary glands, but clinical evidence remains fragmented. This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of MSC therapy for RIX patients.

pmc-13018892.title: VERMONT non-optimised: Feasibility of angiography-derived vFFR using baseline diagnostic catheter images
pmc-13018892.creator: Daniel Akrawi, Krishna Kadappu, James Xu, Tamer Yousef Naguib Badie, Oliver Gibbs, Hashim Kachwalla, Phong TD Nguyen, Rahul Kurup, Upul Premawardhana, Sidney Lo, Justyn Huang, Hao Tran, Kavie Soosapilla, Aiden O’loughlin, Annemarie Hennessy, Giuseppe Femia
pmc-13018892.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundVessel-fractional-flow-reserve (vFFR) estimates coronary physiology from the three-dimensional reconstruction of two angiographic projections using computational fluid dynamics. Although its diagnostic accuracy using optimised angiographic acquisitions is well established, evidence supporting its use with baseline diagnostic catheter images remains limited.AimsTo evaluate the diagnostic performance of real-time vFFR derived from baseline diagnostic catheter images against wire-based FFR, and to compare its performance with vFFR computed from optimised angiographic projections.MethodsVERMONT Non-Optimised was a prospective, single-centre, blinded study in which real-time vFFR derived from both baseline

pmc-13057075.title: Explainable and secure federated learning for privacy-enhancing skin cancer classification using a lightweight multi-scale CNN
pmc-13057075.creator: Abdullah Siddique Mohammad Sayeed, Shaikh Afnan Birahim, Md Shafiq Ullah, Yamina Islam, Avijit Paul, Mohammad Asif Hasan, Mominul Ahsan, Marcin Kowalski
pmc-13057075.description: Skin diseases pose a major public health challenge, with skin cancer being the most prevalent malignancy. Early detection is critical for improving patient outcomes, yet traditional diagnostic methods rely on expert evaluation, which is limited by clinician variability, image quality, and accessibility constraints.

pmc-13071992.title: Multi-Omics Revealed Breed Dominates over Plumage Color in Regulating Pigeon Meat Quality and Flavor
pmc-13071992.creator: Yuanxin Guan, Fei Ye, Xiaofei Xu, Jixiang Wei, Shen Liu, Miaomiao Yang, Jing Wang, Zhengsheng Li, Hai Xiang
pmc-13071992.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummaryMeat quality and flavor are key factors influencing consumer preference for pigeon meat, but it remains unclear whether differences arise from breed or merely from feather color variants within a breed. By comparing white- and grey-feathered Shiqi pigeons with a European breed (Mimas white pigeon) using advanced molecular techniques, we found that breed overwhelmingly determines meat characteristics such as tenderness, fat content, and flavor compounds.

pmc-13161648.title: Identifying individual, community and country-level determinants of poor knowledge of mother-to-child transmission of HIV among women in sub-Saharan Africa: spatial and multilevel analysis
pmc-13161648.creator: Mihret Getnet, Lamrot Yohannes, Nigusu Worku, Adina Yeshambel Belay, Lakew Asmare, Demiss Mulatu Geberu, Asebe Hagos, Melak Jejaw, Misganaw Guadie Tiruneh, Kaleb Assegid Demissie, Yawkal Tsega, Abel Endawkie, Amare Mesfin Workie, Wubshet Debebe Negash
pmc-13161648.description: BackgroundMother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV accounts for over 90% of new HIV infections among children. In 2018, a report from the World Health Organization showed that about 14.8 million children between the ages of 0 and 14 years were HIV-exposed globally, of which 13.2 million reside in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).

pmc-13355003.title: A bidirectional virtual teaching platform for postgraduate Point-of-Care Ultrasound training: a proof-of-concept study
pmc-13355003.creator: Aanchal Ralhan, Queen Jacques, Alison MacDonald, Gillian Sheppard, Peter Rogers, Jordan Stone-McLean

pmc-13364137.creator: Oluwatoyin Favour Olu-Olusegun, Aidan Farrell, James Monaghan, Peter Kettlewell

pmc-13601045.title: Impact of ethanol on odor detection thresholds relevant to No- and Low-Alcohol (NoLo) wines: a combined sensory and computational approach in simplified static hydroalcoholic model wine
pmc-13601045.creator: Laura Brian, Anthony Santacreu, Come de Tournadre, Michel Malcor de Pierrefeu, Jeanne Laronche, Jean-Stéphane Condoret, Audrey Devatine, Séverine Camy, Olivier Geffroy
pmc-13601045.description: The effect of ethanol on odor detection thresholds (ODTs) in fully and partially dealcoholized (NoLo) wines remains largely unexplored. This study used a combined sensory and thermodynamic approach in simplified static hydroalcoholic wine model systems at 0, 6, and 12 % v/v ethanol with three aroma compounds. Orthonasal ODTs were measured using a 3-AFC ascending method.

pmc-13649571.title: Cancer treatment alters mutant selection in normal esophagus
pmc-13649571.creator: Joanna C Fowler, Giuseppina Arbore, Roshan K Sood, Irina Abnizova, Luca Albarello, Oliver Pickering, Kasumi Murai, Ujjwal Banerjee, Salomé Brunon, Swee Hoe Ong, Andrea Cossu, Ugo Elmore, Francesco Puccetti, David Fernandez-Antoran, Giovanni Tonon, Paolo Dellabona, Riccardo Rosati, Samuel Luke Hill,
pmc-13649571.description: Aging epithelial tissues, including the esophagus, are colonized by somatic mutant clones under strong competitive selection. The effect of cancer treatment on mutant selection in normal epithelium is unknown. We hypothesized that some mutant clones may be selectively expanded during treatment. To test this, we sequenced normal esophageal epithelium removed from 70 patients after therapy for esophageal cancer.
